content: The document titled Costing Guidelines for Tuberculosis Interventions was authored by Lucy Cunnama, Inés Garcia Baena, Gabriela Gomez, Yoko Laurence, Carol Levin, Mariana Siapka, Sedona Sweeney, Anna Vassall, and Edina Sinanovic, among others. It was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2019 under the ISBN 978-92-4-000009-4. The guidelines were developed by a core writing team comprising experts from institutions such as the University of Cape Town, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and the University of Washington. The team collaborated with the Global Health Cost Consortium (GHCC) and received funding from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. The guidelines were shaped by feedback from the Value TB project research groups in Ethiopia, Georgia, India, Kenya, and the Philippines, who were the first to use the guidelines. Special acknowledgment is given to Katherine Floyd for her inspiration and support in developing these guidelines. The document provides a structured approach to estimating the costs of delivering tuberculosis (TB) interventions. It is intended for experienced cost data producers who may be less familiar with costing TB services. The guidelines are TB-specific and adaptable to various contexts and purposes. They guide users from protocol design to cost data analysis, offering practical advice on data collection, analysis, and dissemination. However, they do not address cost savings over time, cost-effectiveness assessments, or economic modeling. Instead, the focus is on producing standardized unit costs for economic cost estimation, budgeting, financial planning, and understanding TB programs. The guidelines are structured into stages of a costing study, including pre-data collection activities, defining interventions, setting up study teams, gaining ethical approval, and establishing study objectives. They also provide tools such as the Value TB Costing Tool Suite, which includes data collection and entry components. These tools can be adapted based on the specific costing protocol developed. The guidelines aim to support National Tuberculosis Programmes (NTPs) and their funders in resource allocation and planning, ensuring efficient and equitable use of resources.
